items.about: Testing strip_ansi and ANSI_SEQUENCES for claims C1-C5

claims.text: After the change, OSC sequences that end with BEL or ST are stripped from the output.
The function accepts str, bytes, or bytearray input and returns a value of the same type as the input.
CSI handling and the ESC(B behavior remain unchanged by this PR.
If an OSC sequence lacks a BEL or ST terminator, the function leaves it and any following text untouched in the output.
The ANSI_SEQUENCES regular expression now contains a named group, which could affect code that uses it directly and expects no groups.

main.c5.regex_pattern:
\x1B            # Sequence starts with ESC, i.e. hex 0x1B
    (?:
        [@-Z\\-_]   # Second byte:
                    #   all 0x40–0x5F range but CSI char, i.e ASCII @A–Z\]^_
    |               # Or
        \[          # CSI sequences, starting with [
        [0-?]*      # Parameter bytes:
                    #   range 0x30–0x3F, ASCII 0–9:;<=>?
        [ -/]*      # Intermediate bytes:
                    #   range 0x20–0x2F, ASCII space and !"#$%&'()*+,-./
        [@-~]       # Final byte
                    #   range 0x40–0x7E, ASCII @A–Z[\]^_`a–z{|}~
    )
